_description: Your tools come in packs. Which packs you have, what each tool does in one sentence, and how a pack is turned off.

about.description: How packs work and how to turn one off.

look.description: Pack look: read, ls, view, stat, grep, glob; look at and search files, change nothing.

change.description: Pack change: write, edit, copy, move, mkdir; make and change files.

delete.description: Pack delete: trash (can be undone), remove (cannot).

shell.description: Pack shell: shell, run_python; run a command, read its output and exit code.

gadgets.description: Pack gadgets: peek_clock, peek_now_time, math, do_task (fold one task of your own history into a summary; agent-fsm only).

events.description: Pack events: clock_register (clock letters to your queue), self_hook (run a program when something happens to you).

todo.description: Pack todo: todo (your own to-do list for a long task: ls, set, add, mark).

self.description: Pack self: self_tools, self_llm, self_system, self_history, self_state, self_ctl; look at and change your own copy.

subagent.description: Pack subagent: subagent (helpers you start yourself), agents_ctl (any agent on your daemon), fork (a copy of yourself for one goal; agent-fsm only).

def.description: Pack def: agent_def (new agent definitions), tools_def (new tools).

mailbox.description: Pack mailbox: mailbox_peek, mailbox_read, mailbox_send; letters between agents.

goal.description: Pack goal: goal (one sentence you keep working on; reminded when you stop by yourself).

json.description: Pack json: json_get, json_ls, json_search, json_len, json_set, json_add, json_del, json_multi_get, json_multi_set; one place of a JSON file at a time by FILE#/POINTER.

jsonx.description: Pack jsonx: jsonx_get, jsonx_ls, jsonx_search, jsonx_set, jsonx_add, jsonx_del, jsonx_multi_get, jsonx_multi_set; JSON tools that follow or resolve $ref/$env.

index.description: Pack index: index_view; see a node through its index, change nothing.

kernel_gate.description: Pack kernel_gate: kernel_gate; be a kernel gate (requests come to you, you decide, a station on you forwards). In no stock definition.

about:
# Tool packs

Your tools are registered pack by pack: each pack is one tool list in $AOS_HOME/lib/packs/<pack>.json, and a definition's tools.json stacks the packs it wants with "$override". agent-fsm has fifteen packs: 55 tools. eca-claude has eight (gadgets, events, self, def, mailbox, json, jsonx, index; no look, change, delete, shell, subagent, goal or todo pack: its CLI has its own file tools, shell, helpers, goals and todo lists) and turns off do_task (agent-fsm only): 34 tools. The subagents of an eca (tools_sub.json) get no jsonx. One more pack, kernel_gate, is in no stock definition: add its tool yourself with self_tools (aos/kernel.json#/gate).

- See where each of your tools comes from: self_tools {"op": "ls", "long": true} (FROM shows lib/packs/<pack>.json).
- Turn one tool off for yourself: self_tools {"op": "rm", "name": "shell"}.
- A whole pack is turned off by removing it from the "$override" list of the definition's tools.json (a person or a definition change, not a tool call).
- A tool whose description starts with `[MCP server NAME]` comes from an external MCP server, not from a stock pack: `aos/cli/mcp_import.json#/where_from`.
look: Pack look: Read-only file tools: read (a text file), ls (a folder), view (a file with its type), stat (facts about one path), grep (search inside files, like grep -rn), glob (find files by name pattern). One node per tool: aos/tools/read.json, aos/tools/ls.json, aos/tools/view.json, aos/tools/stat.json, aos/tools/grep.json, aos/tools/glob.json.
change: Pack change: Editing files: write (whole file), edit (replace exact text), copy, move (also rename), mkdir. One node per tool: aos/tools/write.json, aos/tools/edit.json, aos/tools/copy.json, aos/tools/move.json, aos/tools/mkdir.json.
delete: Pack delete: trash (move into your workspace .trash/, can be moved back) and remove (delete for real; a folder needs recursive). One node per tool: aos/tools/trash.json, aos/tools/remove.json.
shell: Pack shell: shell (one bash command; not a sandbox) and run_python (a short Python program). One node per tool: aos/tools/shell.json, aos/tools/run_python.json.
gadgets: Pack gadgets: Small handy tools: peek_clock (the daemon clock: current cycle and interval_ms; ClockMissing when you have no daemon clock), peek_now_time (current UTC time), math (one arithmetic expression), do_task (agent-fsm only: start a task in your own conversation and end it with a summary that replaces its messages; see aos/me.json#/do_task).
events: Pack events: Things that run later: clock_register (a fixed letter every N cycles; leave out box to wake yourself) and self_hook (run a program when something happens to you).
self: Pack self: Look at and change yourself: self_tools (your tools), self_llm (your brain settings), self_system (your system text), self_state (facts and numbers about you), self_ctl (stop, pause, sleep or remove yourself), self_history (your conversation).
subagent: Pack subagent: Other agents: subagent (agents you start yourself; counted against your quota) and agents_ctl (any agent on your daemon table; not counted), and fork (agent-fsm only: a copy of yourself, settings and whole conversation, for one goal; only its short conclusion comes back; see aos/agents.json#/fork).
def: Pack def: Definitions: agent_def (copy a template into a new agent definition, or check one) and tools_def (make a new tool from the Python skeleton, or check a tool).
mailbox: Pack mailbox: Letters: mailbox_peek (what is waiting, without taking it), mailbox_read (read the oldest), mailbox_send (send one).
goal: Pack goal: goal keeps one sentence you are working on (get, set, done, pause, resume) in your stack. When you stop by yourself (your answer calls no tool) and no letter waits, aos gives you a short "[aos] goal: ..." reminder; done or pause stops the reminders. One node: aos/tools/goal.json.
todo: Pack todo: todo keeps your own to-do list for a long task (ls, set, add, mark) in your stack, outside your history; it is not shown to you by itself, so call ls to see it again. One node: aos/tools/todo.json.
json: Pack json: Plain JSON, one place at a time, the path always `FILE#/POINTER`: json_get (one value), json_ls (what is inside, like ls), json_search (find a key or value), json_len (the length: keys, items or characters), json_set (set a value), json_add (add a key or array item, never overwrite), json_del (delete one); json_multi_get and json_multi_set do several places in one call, one result line each. Values are stored exactly as given; `$ref`/`$env` objects are plain objects. One node per tool: aos/tools/json_get.json, aos/tools/json_ls.json, aos/tools/json_search.json, aos/tools/json_len.json, aos/tools/json_set.json, aos/tools/json_add.json, aos/tools/json_del.json, aos/tools/json_multi_get.json, aos/tools/json_multi_set.json.
jsonx: Pack jsonx: For aos configuration files that use `$ref`/`$env`: jsonx_get, jsonx_ls and jsonx_search (follow, resolve), jsonx_set and jsonx_add (value, text or from; follow, resolve, check), jsonx_del (follow); jsonx_multi_get and jsonx_multi_set do several places in one call, the options set once for all. agent-fsm and eca-claude have it. One node per tool: aos/tools/jsonx_get.json, aos/tools/jsonx_ls.json, aos/tools/jsonx_search.json, aos/tools/jsonx_set.json, aos/tools/jsonx_add.json, aos/tools/jsonx_del.json, aos/tools/jsonx_multi_get.json, aos/tools/jsonx_multi_set.json.
index: Pack index: index_view, see a node through its index (the notes agents keep about what is under it); change an index with the json tools. One node: aos/tools/index_view.json.
kernel_gate: Pack kernel_gate: kernel_gate makes you a kernel gate: other procs send their requests to start or change procs to a mailbox of yours, a kernel station hooked on you holds each one, you are told ("[aos] kernel_hold: ...") and decide with op pass or op refuse, and the station forwards what you pass. Not in any stock definition; add it with self_tools {"op": "add", "path": "<AOS_HOME>/lib/agent/kernel_gate"}. See aos/kernel.json#/gate.
